clue.text: An instructor can bring out a diver's potential

indicators.note: the letters of the words a diver's are only potentially the answer, needing to be rearranged into it

explanation.surface: A coach can draw out the latent talent of a diver.
explanation.walkthrough: 'potential' signals that the letters of A DIVERS must be rearranged; the possessive apostrophe adds no letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who instructs also counsels and guides, which is what such a person does.

clue.text: Genial but noisy sailing man dropped in the drink

indicators.note: one thing dropped into another is placed inside it, so these pieces go inside the drink

parts.note: ale is a drink
ff (fortissimo) is the musical mark for very loud
AB, able seaman, is a sailor

explanation.surface: A friendly but loud sailor fell overboard into the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the drink' looks like the sea a sailor falls into, but it is a beer; 'dropped in' puts the loud mark and the seaman inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe a pleasant, approachable and good-natured manner.

clue.text: Bewildering relatives — so changeable

indicators.note: bewildering things are muddled and confused, so the letters of relatives are jumbled

explanation.surface: Confusing relations who keep changing their minds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bewildering' signals that the letters of RELATIVES are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Something adaptable can turn to many uses or moods, so it shifts and alters readily.

clue.text: Locates spectacles for speaker

indicators.note: a speaker heard saying the word produces the sound wanted, so it is a homophone

parts.note: spectacles are things to see, sights

explanation.surface: Someone finds glasses for a person giving a talk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spectacles' looks like glasses but means sights, which said out loud sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To place or position something is to set it at a particular spot.

clue.text: The publication of news must be bang on time

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece written on another sits above it, so the bang comes first

parts.note: a report is a loud bang, as from a gun
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: A news story has to be released exactly when promised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bang on time' reads as 'punctual'; in a down clue 'on' just stacks one piece above the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Journalistic coverage of events is the reporting of current affairs.

clue.text: Breakaway winger

parts.note: sounds like a sports winger who breaks away from the pack, but the winger is a large bird whose name begins with a word meaning break

explanation.surface: A rugby or football wing player escaping the defence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'winger' suggests a sports player; here it is a bird, and 'Breakaway' hints at BUST, to break, at its start.
explanation.definitionFit: A bustard is a big ground-dwelling bird of open plains, so a creature with wings.

clue.text: Having no money, shivered

definitions.meaning: shattered into pieces, as glass is shivered

explanation.surface: A penniless person trembling with cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shivered' looks like trembling, but here means shattered, the past tense of break.
explanation.definitionFit: Penniless people are said to be skint; and to shatter something is to smash it into fragments.

clue.text: Question the head's orthodoxy

parts.note: to sound someone out is to question them
a ness is a headland, a head of land jutting into the sea

explanation.surface: Challenge the headteacher's traditional beliefs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' looks like a headteacher, but is NESS, a promontory, as in Loch Ness or Sheerness place names.
explanation.definitionFit: Doctrine that is correct and reliable is called sound, so its quality is correctness of belief.

clue.text: The absentee's excuse

parts.note: the plea of someone accused who claims to have been elsewhere, absent from the scene, at the time

explanation.walkthrough: 'absentee' suggests someone skipping work; the excuse is the Latin word for 'elsewhere', a defence in court.
explanation.definitionFit: The defence that a suspect was somewhere else when a crime happened.

clue.text: Hung about to fish in divine surroundings

indicators.note: the divine is placed around the fishing word, surrounding it

parts.note: DD, Doctor of Divinity, stands for a clergyman or divine
to angle is to fish with rod and line

explanation.surface: Someone loitered, going fishing with a clergyman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'divine' looks like an adjective but is a noun, a cleric, abbreviated DD.
explanation.definitionFit: Something suspended loosely swinging is hanging around, as a dangling rope does.

clue.text: Deal with a really good man — tip-top!

parts.note: deal is timber of fir or pine
ST, saint, is a very good man

explanation.surface: Doing business with an excellent person is excellent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deal' looks like a verb, but is the wood FIR.
explanation.definitionFit: Top-quality, first-class: the highest ranking.

clue.text: Favouring a -merger which would mean a lot

parts.note: pro means in favour of
fusion is a merger or joining together

explanation.surface: Supporting a corporate merger that would mean a great deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a lot' reads as part of the sentence, but it is the definition, abundance.
explanation.definitionFit: An abundance or great quantity of something is plenty.

clue.text: A sovereign entering a club or restaurant

indicators.note: the sovereign goes into the club, so it is placed inside it

parts.note: a brassie is an old golf club, a wooden two-wood
ER, Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A monarch walks into a nightclub or eatery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sovereign' tempts as a gold coin, but is ER; 'club' is the golf club BRASSIE, not a nightclub.
explanation.definitionFit: A brasserie is an informal French-style eating place serving simple food.

clue.text: A baboon's training for military purposes

explanation.surface: A monkey being trained for the army.
explanation.walkthrough: Two meanings of the same word: an African monkey and marching practice.
explanation.definitionFit: The animal is a forest baboon related to the mandrill; and soldiers practise marching on the parade ground.

clue.text: Get along without 9

parts.note: ex means without, as in ex dividend
the answer to 9 across, abbreviated with a numeral one as 1ST, read as letters

explanation.surface: Manage to survive without coming top.
explanation.walkthrough: '9' points at 9 across, written as the abbreviation 1ST, with the numeral 1 read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: To get along is to live or survive, to be.

clue.text: On which the chartist records current rises and falls

definitions.text: On which the chartist records current rises and falls

parts.words: On which the chartist records current rises and falls
parts.note: chartist suggests a stock-market analyst plotting prices, but the current is sea water and the chart lists times of high and low water

explanation.walkthrough: 'chartist' and 'current' suggest share prices or electricity; this is the sea's ebb and flow.
explanation.definitionFit: A published schedule of high and low water times for a coastal place.

clue.text: Detain suspect

explanation.surface: Arrest the suspect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suspect' looks like a noun, the person arrested, but is a verb, to fear or sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Police arrest a criminal; and to sense or perceive danger coming is to fear it.

clue.text: Retractions written by a friend in verses

parts.note: a pal is a friend
odes are poems, verses

explanation.surface: Withdrawals of statements composed by a friend in poetic form.
explanation.walkthrough: A palinode is a poem retracting something said in an earlier poem.
explanation.definitionFit: A palinode is a recantation, a withdrawal of something earlier said, often in verse.

clue.text: Cut without hesitation — and it's worked!

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the cut word goes around the hesitation

parts.note: excised means cut out
er is a sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: An edit made smoothly, and it succeeded!
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking', but here has its old sense of outside, so the cut wraps around the hesitation.
explanation.definitionFit: Muscles or a body that have been put through training have been exercised, or used.

clue.text: Veronica is fly — with reason

parts.note: to fly is to go fast, to speed
well can mean with good reason, as in you may well ask

explanation.surface: A girl called Veronica is sharp, and with good reason.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Veronica' looks like a woman's name, but is the botanical genus of a small blue-flowered plant.
explanation.definitionFit: The plant genus Veronica is the common name of this small blue-flowered garden flower.

clue.text: Reinstate 26 as capital protection

parts.note: stet is the proofreader's instruction to restore a deleted word
26 across means offspring, of which a son is one

explanation.surface: Restore the matter as main defence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' means the head, so 'capital protection' is a hat; 26 across means offspring, giving SON.
explanation.definitionFit: A wide-brimmed cowboy hat covers and shades the head.

clue.text: Quiet little chap's projection

parts.note: sh is a call for quiet
an elf is a small sprite, a little fellow

explanation.surface: A small quiet man's plan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'projection' suggests a forecast; it is a ledge sticking out from a wall.
explanation.definitionFit: A ledge jutting out from a wall or cliff is an outcrop or ledge.

clue.text: Hold back because of shoulder

parts.note: for can mean because of, as in jumped for joy
to shoulder a burden is to bear it

explanation.surface: Restrain yourself because of an injured shoulder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shoulder' looks like a body part but is a verb, to carry.
explanation.definitionFit: To refrain or abstain from doing something is to restrain oneself.

clue.text: Take in about a hundred pounds for brilliant display

indicators.note: the take-in word is placed about the others, around them

parts.note: to eat is to take in food
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
L, from Latin libra, is the abbreviation for pounds

explanation.surface: Earn about a hundred quid for a dazzling show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'approximately', but places EAT around C and L.
explanation.definitionFit: Showy success or dazzling effect, from the French word for burst or flash.

clue.text: Shortly before midday everybody mounted an animal

indicators.note: in a down clue mounted means climbing upwards, so the word is read from the bottom up

parts.note: am, ante meridiem, is the short form for before noon
all means everybody

explanation.surface: Just before noon everybody climbed onto a beast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mounted' in a down clue turns the whole run AM then ALL upside down, giving LLA MA; 'Shortly' says the time is abbreviated.
explanation.definitionFit: A South American woolly pack animal related to the camel.

clue.text: Exercising care no nun appears as speaker on TV

indicators.note: exercising puts things through movement, so the letters are moved about

explanation.surface: Carefully, no nun appears as a television presenter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exercising' signals rearranging the letters of CARE NO NUN.
explanation.definitionFit: A presenter who introduces programmes or reads continuity on television.

clue.text: A bit detached

parts.note: a part is a bit of something

explanation.surface: Somewhat aloof.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A bit' reads as 'somewhat', but splits into A and PART.
explanation.definitionFit: Separated or set at a distance from each other.

clue.text: Join in the fun — it encourages sociability

indicators.note: the answer is found in the run of letters of the words that follow

explanation.surface: Take part in the fun, as it promotes friendliness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Join in' reads as one phrasal verb, but 'Join' is the definition and 'in' points into fUN ITE ncourages.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring together or combine is to link or connect.

clue.text: Not left afloat

parts.note: reads as not stranded on the water, but means the side that is not the left one on a ship

explanation.walkthrough: 'left' looks like 'abandoned'; it is port, the left side of a ship, and the opposite is wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: The right-hand side of a vessel looking forward is the opposite of port.

clue.text: Put out — is to go to court

parts.note: to sue is to take legal action in court

explanation.surface: Annoyed, someone is heading for legal action.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put out' looks like 'annoyed', but means publish or release.
explanation.definitionFit: To publish or release, as a magazine or statement is circulated.

clue.text: Exceptionally earnest characters, as close as can be

indicators.note: exceptionally suggests something out of the usual order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Very serious people, as intimate as possible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exceptionally' signals rearranging the letters of EARNEST; 'characters' says letters are being used.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of near, meaning closest in distance.

clue.text: Feeble transmitter is out of line

indicators.note: the transmitter lies out of, outside, the line, so it wraps around it

parts.note: a sender transmits signals

explanation.surface: A weak radio signal is off its proper course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of line' reads as misbehaving, but means SENDER outside L.
explanation.definitionFit: Slight or thin, as a slim chance is a weak one.
